rare_regions.activation_trigger: Asynchronous reset (resetn deasserted) or FSM entering IDLE; occurs during system reset or re-initialization.
rare_regions.description: Reset branch clears the received_data register. Reset paths are typically rare (only on power-up or explicit reset) and are important initialization regions. The branch that zeroes received_data when fsm_state == FSM_IDLE is also only taken at idle entry and thus executes infrequently compared to the main receive loop.

rare_regions.rare_region_code:
assign uart_rx_break = uart_rx_valid && ~|received_data;
assign uart_rx_valid = fsm_state == FSM_STOP && n_fsm_state == FSM_IDLE;
rare_regions.activation_trigger: Transition from FSM_STOP to FSM_IDLE (byte/frame completion) and received_data being all zeros for break detection.
rare_regions.description: uart_rx_valid becomes true only when the FSM is finishing reception (FSM_STOP -> FSM_IDLE). This byte-complete event is relatively infrequent compared to the continuous clocking logic. uart_rx_break is true only when a valid byte is detected and the received payload is all zeros — a UART BREAK condition which is an uncommon special-case.

rare_regions.activation_trigger: fsm_state taking an undefined value not covered by explicit cases (default branch).
rare_regions.description: The default case in the FSM is a fallback that forces the next state to FSM_IDLE. Reaching the default case indicates an unexpected or invalid FSM state and is therefore rare; it's an error-recovery / safety path.

rare_regions.activation_trigger: Either system reset, or when uart_rx_en is asserted to enable sampling of uart_rxd.
rare_regions.description: Sampling of the serial input is gated by uart_rx_en. The reset branch sets default idle levels and occurs rarely. The sampling branch executes only when uart_rx_en is high — if that enable is normally low, this path is infrequent. This block also contains initialization on reset (rare).

rare_regions.rare_region_code:
always @(posedge clk) begin : p_cycle_counter
    if(!resetn) begin
        cycle_counter <= {COUNT_REG_LEN{1'b0}};
    end else if(next_bit) begin
        cycle_counter <= {COUNT_REG_LEN{1'b0}};
    end else if(fsm_state == FSM_START || 
                fsm_state == FSM_RECV  || 
                fsm_state == FSM_STOP   ) begin
        cycle_counter <= cycle_counter + 1'b1;
    end
end
rare_regions.activation_trigger: next_bit condition (cycle_counter reaches CYCLES_PER_BIT or middle-of-stop condition) causing counter reset; occurs once per received bit timing interval.
rare_regions.description: The next_bit condition triggers counter reset and is evaluated at baud-timing boundaries. Although it occurs repeatedly during an active byte reception, it is infrequent relative to per-clock activity (only at bit boundaries) and is a timing-sensitive path (potentially interesting as a rare-event boundary). The reset branch is also rare.
